data.title: Borr Drilling to sell 51% stake in two Mexican joint ventures
data.description:
• Borr Drilling (BORR) has agreed to sell its 51% stake in two Mexican joint ventures to its long-standing local partner in the country.
  • Upon completion of the transaction, Borr Drilling will have fully divested Perfomex, while its local partner will become the sole owner of Perfomex and assume responsibility for the management and operation of the company's jack-up rigs Galar, Gersemi and Njord, which are currently operating with PEMEX.
  • The company will retain ownership of the three rigs and continue participating in the underlying contracts through bareboat charter agreements, with economics expected to be largely unchanged from the existing arrangement.
  • Njord is currently contracted through April 2028, with extension options thereafter, while Galar and Gersemi are contracted through May 2030.
  • Following completion of the transaction, Perfomex will continue its operations related to integrated well services and PEMEX, while Borr Drilling will independently operate and market its fleet to other operators in the region through its affiliated companies.
  • The transaction is expected to simplify Borr Drilling's corporate and operating structure in Mexico.

data.title: Micware partners with ESRI Japan on urban, mobility and infrastructure data
data.description:
• Micware (MWC) has entered into a business alliance with ESRI Japan to develop and commercialize spatial information infrastructure that can continuously capture and analyze changes in the physical world, with applications spanning cities, mobility, roads, and infrastructure.
  • Micware will provide technology that collects location and video data, while ESRI Japan will use its ArcGIS platform to organize, display, and analyze the information.
  • The companies will also work on digital models of cities and solutions that use data from vehicles to monitor road conditions, traffic, and surrounding areas. The partnership is part of Micware’s DynaPlanet-PF spatial intelligence strategy. Micware established Micware Spacia on September 1 to expand its spatial intelligence business.
  • No financial terms, contract value, revenue contribution, or earnings impact was disclosed.
  • ESRI Japan participated in Micware’s May 14 IPO and acquired Micware’s American depositary shares. The value of the investment was not disclosed.

data.title: Moody’s takes minority stake in PhilRatings
data.description:
Moody’s (MCO) has agreed to acquire a minority stake in Philippine Rating Services (PhilRatings), a domestic credit rating agency in the Philippines.

The investment expands Moody’s Asia-Pacific network of domestic rating agency affiliates.

“Strong domestic debt markets are essential to supporting sustainable economic growth,” said Wendy Cheong, Managing Director and Regional Head of Asia Pacific, Moody’s Ratings. “PhilRatings has built deep insight into the local market, and its ratings serve as a strong complement to Moody’s global views on credit for investors in the Philippines.”

Following Moody’s investment, PhilRatings will continue to operate independently with its own management, governance, and credit rating processes.

data.title: France inflation accelerates to 2.4% in August
data.description:
• The annual inflation rate in France accelerated to 2.4% in August, up from 2.1% in July and confirming preliminary estimates.
  • This marked the highest reading in three months, driven mainly by a sharp acceleration in energy inflation to 16.7% from 12.6% in July, particularly for petroleum products. 
  • The consumer prices in France rose 0.7% from a month earlier in August 2026, confirming preliminary estimates.

data.title: Ascendis Pharma sets $400M stock buyback plan
data.description:
• Ascendis Pharma (ASND) board has authorized the company to repurchase up to $400M of its ordinary shares.
  • The program does not require the company to repurchase any specific number of shares, and may be modified, suspended, or terminated at any time without notice.

data.title: TotalEnergies, Mistral team up on frontier AI for reservoir exploration
data.description:
• TotalEnergies (TTE) and Mistral reported a 3-year joint program representing an investment of more than €100 million aimed at developing a new generation of frontier AI models to support TotalEnergies’ geosciences experts in the exploration, characterization, and development of oil and gas reservoirs.
  • This partnership will draw on the latest advances in artificial intelligence, particularly agentic AI, to combine next to 10 petaflops of data with nearly a century of knowledge, know-how, and expertise accumulated by TotalEnergies in geosciences and reservoir engineering.
  • The objective is to develop new frontier models able to integrate, process, and interpret large volumes of data to generate multiple scenarios for the development of exploration opportunities, as well as for optimizing and extending the life of existing projects.
  • Mistral AI  raised a record €3 billion in funding this month, backed by Samsung, Nvidia, and BlackRock.

data.title: S&P 500 faces 8%-10% pullback risk as Fed rate hikes loom, strategist says
data.description:
Potential Federal Reserve rate hikes starting this week could trigger an 8% to 10% correction in the S&P 500 (SP500), as higher borrowing costs squeeze corporate margins, weigh on earnings outlooks, and expose markets to a tightening cycle, according to Macro Risk Advisors LLC.

“We expect an 8-10% pullback in S&P with a potential second leg in December,” said Dean Curnutt, chief executive officer and founder of Macro Risk Advisors, in a Monday note to clients, according to Bloomberg.

Rate hikes will “compress margins in companies that cannot pass costs through” and deliver a volatility shock to a market that is not positioned for it, Curnutt added.

The S&P 500 has fallen nearly 1% so far in September, historically its weakest month, amid concerns over elevated energy costs and recent inflation data that pushed the 10-year U.S. Treasury yield to its highest level in nearly two decades.

Traders are now almost fully pricing in a quarter-point rate hike by Fed Chairman Kevin Warsh on Wednesday, up from about 60% odds a week ago. A rate hike on Wednesday is likely to lead to more pain, Curnutt said.

Curnutt said the current setup resembles 2018, when the S&P 500 peaked in September before plunging 10% over October and November. That year, Curnutt warned, “The Santa Claus rally did not come,” and the market took another leg lower in December, eventually falling nearly 20% from its peak.

Given that history, “a defensive posture is the correct approach,” he said. Similar to 2018, he expects the market to take another leg lower in December as multiple Fed hikes hit “into a K-shaped, low-churn economy.”

The S&P 500 is heavily concentrated in mega-cap technology and AI-related stocks, with Nvidia (NVDA), Apple (AAPL), Microsoft (MSFT), Amazon (AMZN), Alphabet (GOOGL/GOOG), Broadcom (AVGO), Meta Platforms (META), and Tesla (TSLA) among its largest constituents.

NVDA has fallen over 4% so far in September, AMZN is down 2.4%, AVGO -6.9%, and TSLA has dipped 2.4%. AAPL is up 5%, while GOOG has gained 3% in the month so far.

data.title: China steps up safeguards against AI losing human control
data.description:
China is stepping up safeguards against the risk of increasingly powerful AI systems escaping human control, as Beijing seeks to manage the technology without slowing its rapid development.

The issue has gained urgency after Anthropic (ANTHRO) CEO Dario Amodei called for AI companies to slow the pace of model development, while Anthropic (ANTHRO) has reported cases involving AI models being used for cyber weapons, and other high-risk activities.

Beijing has also warned about frontier models bypassing safety controls and attacking external systems. China’s state security minister, Chen Yixin, has separately warned that advanced U.S. AI models could threaten the country’s critical information infrastructure.

Chinese regulators in May identified “operational loss of control” as a security risk for autonomous AI agents and required developers to detect, block, and recover from improper behavior while keeping humans responsible for final decisions. 

China first included AI “loss of control” scenarios in a 2024 safety framework, with a 2025 update warning that AI could experience a sudden jump in intelligence before acquiring resources, replicating itself, and seeking power.

Beijing, however, is not advocating a broad slowdown. Instead, it is pairing rapid AI deployment with regulation, technical standards, and state oversight. China also pushed back this week against U.S. calls to restrict AI development, with Foreign Ministry spokesman Guo Jiakun warning that “fearmongering” and confrontation would undermine global AI governance.

data.title: Waymo aims to launch robotaxi service in Tokyo in 2027
data.description:
Alphabet-owned (GOOG) Waymo (WAYMO), Japanese ride-hailing app GO and taxi operator Nihon Kotsu are targeting to launch Japan's first fully autonomous robotaxi service in Tokyo in 2027.

"This timeline is contingent on securing regulatory approval from national and local authorities, as well as completing the ongoing validation of Waymo's technology and our joint operations," the companies noted.

The service will launch with an initial fleet before gradually expanding to around 100 vehicles across key Tokyo neighborhoods.

Once launched, people can hail robotaxi rides through both the GO and Waymo (WAYMO) apps.

"We'll grow our fleet responsibly over time, steadily operating until anyone in Tokyo can download an app and take ​a ride," Waymo (WAYMO) Co-CEO Tekedra Mawakana ‌said during a joint press conference in Tokyo.

Yasuharu Wakabayashi, president of Nihon Kotsu, said the service "will help address future driver shortages and pass on a safer, higher-quality transportation infrastructure to the next generation."

Waymo (WAYMO) began collecting road data in Tokyo last year by using manually-driven rides in its first international expansion.

data.title: U.S. 10-year Treasury yield climbs to highest level since 2007 ahead of Fed decision
data.description:
The 10-year U.S. Treasury yield (US10Y) climbed to its highest level in nearly two decades, extending a global bond selloff driven by surging energy prices, rising debt, and inflation concerns.

The benchmark yield rose as much as 4 basis points from the session low of 4.99% to 5.03% on Tuesday, surpassing its 2023 peak and reaching its highest level since 2007. On Monday, the 10-year yield had briefly crossed 5%, before sliding a little.

The latest move followed a rise in global oil prices as risks to Middle East energy supplies increased.

The bond-market selloff adds pressure ahead of the Federal Reserve’s interest-rate decision Wednesday, with investors expecting officials to raise short-term borrowing costs for the first time since July 2023.

If the Fed does not hike, or if Fed Chairman Kevin Warsh signals less tightening ahead than currently priced into money markets, bond investors could demand even higher yields to compensate for rising inflation risks.

The rise extended across the Treasury curve, with the rate-sensitive U.S. 2-Year Treasury yield (US2Y) gaining 3 basis points to about 4.69%, while the U.S. 30-Year Treasury yield (US30Y) climbed 4 basis points to 5.39%.
